title: Raptor: Rejection-aware Adaptive Tree based on Speculative Decoding
abstract: arXiv:2611.25436v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Tree-structured speculative decoding accelerates vision-language models (VLMs) by verifying multiple candidate continuations in parallel. However, long visual contexts increase the cost of speculative computation, making candidate coverage and redundant expansion important considerations beyond tree topology adaptation. We propose Raptor, a training-free framework that uses rejection feedback to jointly regulate candidate coverage and drafting effort. Our key insight is that acceptance length alone cannot distinguish insufficient candidate coverage from excessive deep expansion, and these conditions require different allocation decisions. Raptor therefore extracts complementary rejection-aware signals to characterize speculative progress, frontier coverage, and redundant expansion. translated_title: Raptor：基于投机解码的拒绝感知自适应树
translated_abstract: 树结构投机解码通过并行验证多个候选延续来加速视觉语言模型（VLM）的推理。然而，长视觉上下文会增加投机计算的成本，使得候选覆盖率与冗余扩展成为树拓扑自适应之外需要重点考量的问题。我们提出了 Raptor，一个免训练的框架，它利用拒绝反馈来联合调控候选覆盖率与草稿生成开销。我们的关键洞察是：仅凭接受长度无法区分“候选覆盖率不足”与“过度深度扩展”这两种情况，而这两种情况需要不同的资源分配决策。因此，Raptor 提取互补的拒绝感知信号，用以刻画投机进度、前沿覆盖率与冗余扩展。这些信号共同引导对树深度、分支宽度和草稿预算进行有界的、动量平滑的更新，并结合执行控制来限制……
tldr: Raptor 提出了一种免训练的拒绝感知自适应树投机解码框架，通过从拒绝反馈中提取互补信号来联合调控候选覆盖率与草稿开销，从而高效加速视觉语言模型的推理。
en_tdlr: Raptor is a training-free, rejection-aware adaptive tree speculative decoding framework that extracts complementary rejection-feedback signals to jointly regulate candidate coverage and drafting effort, thereby efficiently accelerating vision-language model inference.
